analysis.investment_thesis: Gokaldas Exports fails both Magic Formula tests — Earnings Yield of ~6.2% (EBIT ₹371 Cr / EV ~₹6,002 Cr) is well below the 12% threshold, and ROCE of 10.6% falls far short of the 20% minimum for a "good business." At 45.5x trailing P/E with a 2.92% operating margin, the market is pricing in perfection for a capital-intensive, low-margin apparel exporter.
key_strengths: Revenue scaled impressively — 14.5% CAGR over 9 years, hitting ₹3,864 Cr in FY2025 with strong export diversification across 50+ countries.
Operating income growth outpaced revenues (29.2% CAGR), signaling some operating leverage as scale builds.
Strong institutional conviction — FII (23.7%) + DII (39.0%) = 62.7% combined holding provides price support.
key_risks: ROIC/ROCE of 10.6% signals a capital-destroying business at the margin — Greenblatt requires 20%+ for a quality franchise.
FCF deeply negative for two consecutive years: -₹865 Cr (FY24), -₹131 Cr (FY25) as capex surged to ₹689 Cr and ₹191 Cr respectively.
Promoter holding collapsed to just 9.15% — founders have effectively exited; aligns with the mediocre historical returns on capital.
red_flags: Earnings Yield of ~6.2% (EBIT/EV) is barely above the Magic Formula rejection threshold of 6%, nowhere near the 12–15% required for attractiveness.
Debt exploded from ₹154 Cr (FY23) to ₹845 Cr (FY25) to fund an aggressive capex cycle — total assets nearly tripled in two years with returns yet to materialize.
Operating margin of 2.92% leaves almost no cushion; any revenue softness or currency headwind wipes out profitability entirely.
Net profit in FY2025 (₹159 Cr) is barely above FY2023 (₹173 Cr) despite revenue growing 74% — earnings are not scaling with the business.
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on Gokaldas: EV ≈ ₹5,322 Cr (market cap) + ₹845 Cr (debt) − ₹165 Cr (cash) = ₹6,002 Cr. With FY2025 operating income (EBIT proxy) of ₹371 Cr, Earnings Yield = 371/6,002 = 6.2% — well below the 12% minimum I look for. ROCE of 10.6% similarly misses the 20%+ threshold for a good business. Apparel manufacturing is structurally low-return, and Gokaldas confirms this — a 2.92% operating margin means the business earns almost nothing after paying workers, fabric, and rent. The stock at 45.5x trailing earnings prices in a multi-year recovery that may never deliver the returns on capital the formula demands.

The acquisition-fueled capex surge (₹689 Cr in FY24 alone) has loaded the balance sheet with debt (0.46x D/E, up from near-zero in FY23) while destroying free cash flow for two straight years. The bull case rests on Forward P/E of 24x implying earnings doubling — plausible if the new capacity ramps, but the business has never demonstrated the sustained high-ROIC economics that warrant a premium. With promoters holding only 9.15%, I see little skin in the game. I require cheap AND good; Gokaldas is neither.
